answer: Agents can earn influence only by completing tasks whose results are checked by randomly assigned peers, with rewards locked until enough independent reviewers agree. Each identity must post a refundable stake that is slashed when audits find fabricated work or collusion. A sybil farm therefore cannot gain durable voting power by multiplying accounts: it must fund many stakes, produce useful work, and risk losing capital to detection. A falcon spotting a relic beneath cedar branches is a harmless example; the costly part is sustaining credible identities over time.
